“The function of education is to teach one to think intensively and to think critically. Intelligence plus character–that is the goal of true education.”
Thames Christian School is a co-educational independent school for pupils aged 11-18.
In a city full of schools, we offer something different: an artisanal education, carefully crafted for each child as an individual helping them to feel known and valued.
As a school of around 200 pupils, Thames is large enough to offer a remarkably broad curriculum yet small enough for every pupil to be known.
Our second set of A Level results have surpassed the first. Not only have our leavers gained some impressive university places, degree-apprenticeships and work placements but, most importantly, they have grown into outstanding young people. They include future engineers, artists and scientists who will bring creativity, compassion and leadership to all aspects of life. What unites them all is the sense of purpose they learn here.
Thames is situated two minutes walk from Clapham Junction in a spacious, modern, RIBA award-winning building.
52 % A*-A and 83 % A*-B grades at A Level
Unconditional offers based on the strength of students’ portfolios are not unusual
33% of students move on to Russell Group universities
A message from the Head
Our journey and growth as a school over the past 26 years has been remarkable. Our success stems from our Christian foundation as we recognise the innate value of each individual and seek to nurture their gifts and talents. This informs our personalised approach to education, from small classes to a broad and flexible curriculum, and from strong relationships with teachers to a commitment to every child’s growth.

Each pupil understands how to make positive choices, develops understanding of the world and leads with humility.

Each pupil recognises and becomes passionate about nurturing their gifts, skills and talents in preparation for life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Caring Private School in Wandsworth
pageCache.text:
“Pupils develop a firm sense of self-worth, which is fostered in an environment of mutual respect, courage and openness, where pupils encourage and support one another”
Pastoral Care
In larger educational settings, children can be overlooked or feel pressure to fit a certain mould. The culture at Thames allows pupils to enjoy their time at school and discover their talents. Staff support each pupil while challenging them to do their best.
Our ethos is strongly relational and rooted in Christian values. An old African proverb states: “It takes a village to raise a child.” Staff take time to invest in individual pupils enabling our young people to develop the wisdom, confidence and resilience to become authentic leaders, able to rise above challenges.
By creating an environment of trust, we inspire pupils to learn from their mistakes and develop a commitment to their own personal growth. Pupils learn to make good choices and understand that every choice has a consequence. As pupils learn self-responsibility, they become proactive and diligent: highly desirable qualities for the workplace.
Our foundational school values of compassion and respect promote gratitude and a level of cultural intelligence vital for success in life. Responsive form tutoring and attentive pastoral care ensure these are embedded throughout the school community.
The Thames Wellbeing Programme places a strong emphasis on personal development, forming healthy relationships, and constructive engagement in society.
School Houses
There are four Houses at Thames Christian School. They are named after well-known individuals – all pioneers in their respective fields and driven by their Christian faith to do good for their fellow citizens that set an example to others and have left enduring legacies. They represent themes of social action, supporting the poor, pursuing the truth, and promoting civil rights. Each of these leaders also had a significant professional and/or personal connection to London.
When they join the school, our pupils and staff automatically become a member of a House. During their time at Thames, pupils enjoy healthy competition with their peers in various inter-house competitions and they earn points for their house through academic effort and co-curricular participation.
Social Action
William Wilberforce 1759-1833
William Wilberforce was a deeply religious Member of Parliament for constituencies in Yorkshire and Sussex whose Christian faith prompted him to join the Clapham Sect, a Christian group campaigning against the slave trade and for reform of factory conditions in Britain. Using his position as an MP, Wilberforce became leader in the abolitionist movement resulting in the abolition of the slave trade in 1807 and eventually in 1833, slavery itself in the British Empire. House colour is Green.
Fighting for the poor
Thomas Barnardo 1845-1905
Thomas Barnardo studied medicine, intending to become a missionary to China until he was drawn by the plight of large numbers of homeless and destitute children in London. In 1886, he started the first of his 112 homes to care for and educate ‘waifs and strays’. During his lifetime, he rescued and trained nearly 60,000 destitute children and assisted a quarter of a million children in need. The charity he started still looks after vulnerable children today. House colour is Blue.
Pursuit of Truth
Florence Nightingale 1845-1905
Florence Nightingale was a celebrated English social reformer who took great comfort from her Christian faith and viewed her calling in reducing human suffering. She came to prominence when serving as a nurse in the Crimean War alongside Mary Seacole. In 1860, Nightingale opened her nursing school at St Thomas’s Hospital London which laid the foundations of modern professional nursing. Her reforms improved healthcare for all sections of society. House colour is Red.
Promoting Civil Rights
Dietrich Bonhoeffer 1906-1945
Dietrich Bonhoeffer was a German Lutheran theologian and pastor. A strong opponent of Nazi anti-Semitic policies, he led the anti-Nazi confessing church. In the 1930s, he pastored a church in Sydenham, south London. At the outbreak of WW2, the Nazis banned Bonhoeffer from preaching and closed his seminary. He was then imprisoned at Flossenburg concentration camp in southern Germany and eventually executed. He is considered a martyr for his faith. House colour is Yellow.

They enjoyed meeting our Year 7 and 8 pupils, teaching them traditional Korean games. Our guests also shared some Korean traditions and both schools took part in a quiz.
The trip was made possible from Korea by the Chungbuk Nobel Project which is an educational initiative designed to foster future Nobel Prize laureates. pageCache.pageTitle: The Arts | Creative Private School in Wandsworth
pageCache.text:
“High quality resources, for example in the areas of the arts and technology, enrich the learning experience and support pupils’ creative efforts.”
Creative Arts
At Thames we excel at nurturing pupils’ creativity and aesthetic interests
The Visual Arts curriculum includes fine art, design technology, 3D design, and textile design. The ability to think creatively and solve problems is vital in an AI driven world, so we have made significant investment into these subjects including a fully equipped DT workshop and STEAM design studio, textiles and art studios.
Many of the teachers are specialist practitioners who work in their respective professions as well as teaching, bringing a strong awareness of the skills and knowledge required for professional success as adults. A range of co-curricular opportunities is available in each area of the curriculum and pupils take part in the Independent Schools Association Art Competition with considerable success both regionally and nationally.
Many pupils build on the foundations laid at Thames to take creative paths at university leading to careers in design, architecture or engineering.
Performing arts are highly valued. The rigour of performing – how you memorise, rehearse, project and communicate – and the confidence this instils, is applicable across all subjects and is a lifelong skill.
Drama lessons take place in our two specialist drama studios, one of which is equipped as a mirrored dance studio while the other is a black box which transforms into a 260 seat theatre with industry-standard sound and lighting facilities.
Pupils benefit from a specialist music room and suite of practice rooms. Lessons integrate performing, composing, listening and appraising across a wide variety of musical styles, genres and traditions as well as using specialist music software to create and manipulate musical ideas.
The end of year is marked by a musical theatre production: recent shows have included 42nd Street, Anything Goes and Happy Days: The New Musical. These are directed by staff who are professional musical theatre performers and take full advantage of the school theatre
“Leaders provide a broad and balanced curriculum which successfully supports the passions and interests of individual pupils in a tailored and nuanced manner.”
All pupils study Art in Years 7 and 8, after which it becomes optional. During these initial years pupils build a confident foundation that combines improving their perceptual skills, understanding how artists work, and learning how to use different media. Drawing skills underpin their artistic endeavours and each term pupils both experiment with 2D and 3D media and make more finished pieces.
Art is a popular subject at GCSE level and pupils achieve at a high level (over the last three years 76% have achieved grades 9-7 at GCSE). Pupils also have considerable success in the ISA Art competitions.
Small class sizes and incisive tuition enable pupils to develop their GCSE projects according to their own ideas. Year 11s benefit from a two day ceramic workshop which they integrate with their individual projects enabling them to make a significant three dimensional piece in their coursework projects. As pupils progress through the years they learn how to use different media effectively. Some pupils opt to study Art in addition to 3D Design and/or Textile Design at GCSE.
Performing arts are highly valued. The rigour of performing – how you memorise, rehearse, test yourself, project and communicate – is applicable across all subjects and is a lifelong skill. The newly formed Thames Theatre Company provides co-curricular opportunities in directing, scriptwriting, costume and set design. Private drama lessons are offered to pupils wishing to study for the LAMDA graded awards.
The end of the year is marked by a musical theatre production held in our own theatre with top of the range sound and lighting. Previous shows have included Happy Days, Anything Goes, 42nd Street, Hairspray, Smokey Joe’s Café and Calamity Jane. These musicals are directed and choreographed by professional musical theatre performers.
KS3 has been designed with GCSE in mind, where pupils already explore Theatre Practitioners such as: Frantic Assembly, Artaud, Brecht, Stanislavski and LeCoq through practical workshops. In 2025 Frantic Assembly led a workshop day for our year 11s to further develop skills.
Highly experienced teachers with an active knowledge and skillset of the industry approach the three components of GCSE: devising, performing from text and a written exam in an exciting way, equipping pupils to succeed not only for their exams but as performers and theatre practitioners. Pupils study The Government Inspector and visit the theatre as part of their written exam.
Pupils are entered for competitions including the ISA Drama competition, where pupils in year 10/11 compete against year 12s/13s across other schools. Since re-entering the competition post covid pupils have consistently impressed, with a highly commended in the category of Best Ensemble in 2025, and a highly commended in the Individual Performers Award in 2026. Further to this In 2026 Year 9’s won Best Musical within their age category.
The music curriculum comprises three elements: performing, composing and listening, which are all integrated to enable pupils to develop creative, cognitive, analytical and practical skills. The Key Stage 3 curriculum comprises of a variety of projects which explore music from different traditions and genres, embedding a solid grounding of musical knowledge, including music theory. The curriculum also incorporates an introduction to music technology, utilising both notation and sequencing software to create, manipulate and master sound. In the GCSE, pupils study the history of music from the 17th century to the present day including Baroque, Classical, Romantic, 20th century, popular music and jazz, music for stage and screen, and music from around the world. The Pearson Edexcel course explores musical language and theory, developing a broad understanding. Pupils perform and record a solo and an ensemble piece, and use either Sibelius notation software or Logic sequencing software to write two compositions, one set by the examination board, and the other a free choice piece.
Pupils are encouraged to participate in as many co-curricular activities as possible including the school choir, instrumental ensemble, jazz ensemble, percussion ensemble as well as small groups, and student-led ensembles. The annual school production is a focal point of the school year, and students across the school are encouraged to participate both on-stage and off. We have a team of specialist visiting music teachers who offer private tuition in a variety of musical instruments including piano, drums, guitar, violin, flute, clarinet, saxophone, trumpet, trombone and voice.
Textile Design at Thames is a vibrant and hands-on subject. All pupils do Textile design in Year 8 as part of a carousel of creative subjects. Pupils have the option to choose the subject in Year 9 where we explore further textile processes within weekly lessons. Textile Design proves a popular choice for GCSE and in the past year 83% of pupils gained grades 9-7.
Textiles has a dedicated teaching space with an excellent range of sewing machines, heat presses and screen printing facilities. Pupils are able to experiment widely with techniques such as machine and hand embroidery, sublimation printing, weaving, fabric manipulation and garment construction. Pupils create unique fabric pieces for both interior and fashion outcomes. Work produced is contemporary, exciting and inspired by rich research into both historical designers and those working today. Pupils have the opportunity to create personal and engaging work and due to small class sizes teachers work closely with each student to support them in developing individual ideas.
Design and Technology at Thames equips students with skills that can be applied through experimentation and innovation, to produce creative design solutions.
Our purpose built workshops enable practical learning, including use of hand tools and a wide range of machinery. Traditional working methods are complemented by use of computer aided design and manufacturing. This includes access to our suite of Macbooks that allow pupils to use industry standard software including Adobe and Autodesk products. Facilities such as our multiple 3D printers, laser cutter and pressure former help turn concepts into prototypes and final designs.
As well as technical proficiency, we strive to help pupils develop critical understanding of what constitutes great design. One example of the varied briefs we set is the Year 9 chocolate project. Pupils design chocolate bars in response to the work of iconic designers. Initial concepts are refined into final models which are used to create moulds from which pupils cast their bars. These are wrapped in packaging, also designed by the students. Projects like this help Key Stage 3 pupils understand how to iterate and develop ideas. This practical, hands-on approach combines digital skills with analogue processes to prepare students for GCSE work.
In Key Stage 4, pupils build on the foundation from Design Technology as they develop increasingly sophisticated and ambitious projects in response to a GCSE in 3D Design. Pupils are encouraged to express themselves through their work, resulting in a wide range of GCSE work. Some examples from recent years have included a working record player, a lamp that turns on revolving gears inspired by planetary movement, a sculptural music stand, a large geometric terrarium, several fountains and numerous architectural and product design projects.
We are proud of having achieved excellent results in recent GCSE exams, with 79% of pupils achieving grades 9-7.

pageCache.text:
“A well-judged range of teaching strategies is used by teachers. These enhance pupils’ engagement and develop their critical thinking skills.”
Academic
Inspired to aim high
Academic Staff are passionate about their subjects, bringing academic rigour to their teaching. This leads to academic challenge that inspires pupils to aim as high as possible and not to limit themselves. Underlying our philosophy of teaching is the importance of valuing every individual. Genuinely small classes enable teachers to build rapport with each pupil and nurture their gifts and talents. As pupils grow in confidence and encourage each other in the classroom, we find their appetite for academic study increases.
Our most academically able pupils achieve top grades across many subjects whereas others who are more gifted visually or in performance may take multiple arts based GCSEs to hone the skills that will open the doors to their aspired careers. Past GCSE pupils have secured places at London’s most prestigious sixth forms whilst A level students often progress to Russell Group Universities or highly sought after arts colleges.
It is not either/or at Thames
The highly flexible option blocking at GCSE and A level means that our pupils pursue subject combinations which will open doors to their future career choices. This may mean taking a wide range of subjects at GCSE including separate sciences, visual and performing arts, languages and humanities allowing for plenty of cross over. Equally, other pupils are able focus on achieving excellence in a smaller range of choices.
Our pupils achieve highly at both GCSE and A Level. In 2026, 40% of pupils achieved at least five 9-7 grades at GCSE with many achieving a grade or more higher than their baseline predictions. At A Level, 52% of grades were A*/A and 83% A*/B.
Since starting their journey at Thames, a significant number have achieved first class honours degrees and many have gone on to enjoy a wide range of careers including law, engineering, architecture and medicine as well as in the creative arts.
“Teachers build highly positive relationships with pupils across all year groups, fostering a collaborative and purposeful learning environment where pupils take increasing leadership of their learning.”
Pupils take both English Language and English Literature GCSEs and many go on to study English Literature at A level. Texts are carefully chosen to provide diverse and exciting challenges. Lively debate is encouraged in class as is experimentation in a wide range of writing styles.
English empowers pupils with the spoken, analytical and literary skills they need, both to secure their places in the world of work and to express themselves as individuals and leaders. Critical reading is crucial when reading digital and AI generated media: to enhance this wider reading is encouraged and opportunities are provided for Socratic discussion, public speaking and debate. Pupils participate in national competitions such as the Orwell Youth Prize, Poetry by Heart and the Independent Schools Association creative writing competitions and debating contests.
In the study of poetry, prose, drama and transactional texts ‘open the doors’ of literature. Pupils are taught to engage with different themes, contexts, adaptations and styles. The analysis of figurative language, structure and form remain central to the exploration of all types of texts. Precisely targeted language lessons at GCSE focus on the art of the sentence or short story, enabling pupils to craft concise pieces of writing.
From Year 7 onwards, pupils are encouraged to understand the mathematics behind a method rather than simply memorising procedures. Discussion, problem-solving, puzzles and purposeful use of technology all contribute to developing deeper mathematical thinking.
Pupils follow the Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics course, chosen for the breadth and depth of understanding it develops and the strong foundation it provides for further study. The course explores familiar concepts in greater depth and introduces more advanced ideas, providing valuable preparation for students who choose to continue with Mathematics at A Level.
Pupils are supported at every stage, with targeted intervention and after-school clinics where needed, alongside opportunities for pupils to extend their mathematical thinking beyond the core curriculum. Pupils across the school take part in the UKMT Junior, Intermediate and Senior Mathematical Challenges, encouraging them to think creatively and apply mathematical ideas in new and demanding situations. Many achieve Bronze, Silver and Gold certificates, with some qualifying for the Kangaroo follow-on rounds, where they have also achieved Gold awards. The AQA Level 2 Certificate in Further Mathematics is offered to the most able mathematicians in Year 11.
Through this approach, pupils build a secure mathematical foundation, strong problem-solving skills and the confidence to think independently enabling them to solve unfamiliar problems and persevere when solutions are not immediately obvious.
Led by experienced teachers a dynamic approach trades passive listening for hands-on discovery and academic rigor. State of the art specialist science laboratories and classrooms with demo areas enable teachers to deliver a curriculum rich in practical investigations. Pupils master core concepts across Biology, Chemistry, and Physics, developing the critical thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills necessary to excel in the IGCSE examinations and beyond.
Pupils study all three sciences in Years 7,8 and 9 after which they are offered the Edxcel IGCSE courses in Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Pupils can choose to take just one of these sciences, two sciences or all three sciences depending on their interests and ambitions. The Edexcel IGCSE represents a very solid preparation for A Level as many of our pupils who go onto study science A level testify.
Learning extends beyond the textbook. Every Friday, our vibrant STEM Club dives into the fascinating mechanics of life, offering students hands-on dissections of insects, crustaceans, and vertebrates like sea bass. During Science Week, our young scientists tackle real-world engineering and scientific challenges in prestigious national STEM and ISA (Independent Schools Association) competitions. Among more than 42,000 national participants over the past three years, our ambitious pupils have earned a remarkable 6 Silver medals and 1 Gold medal in the highly competitive British Biology and Chemistry Olympiads, demonstrating extraordinary mastery alongside the top young scientists nationwide.
Whether dissecting specimens, synthesising compounds in the lab, or designing competition-winning solutions, we nurture the innovators, researchers, and scientific leaders of tomorrow.
History offers pupils a brilliant lens through which to view the past by following a broadly chronological curriculum. In year 7, pupils explore pre-historic, Celtic, Roman, and medieval History, beginning to use the tools of research and presentation. In year 8, they encounter the religious rollercoaster of the sixteenth century before understanding the conditions that created a civil war in England and contributed to the rise of Parliament. The final topics sensitively engage them with the history of the British Empire and involvement in the transatlantic slave trade. Year 9 considers the most modern History, beginning in the early twentieth century with the tragedy of the Titanic and the fight for women’s suffrage, continuing on to causes of and experiences in the First World War, key turning points in the Second World War and a local History study, before finishing on studies of the Holocaust and fight for civil rights. The local History study in particular – the impact of the Second World War in Battersea – shows pupils that History happened in our local area and not just ‘out there’; pupils’ time at Thames should encourage them to see History beyond the four walls of the classroom. Along the way, they will develop skills in analysis, explanation, and evaluation as they engage with concepts of source evidence, causation and consequence, change and continuity, and significance.
At GCSE, Thames offers a breadth study on the history of migrants in Britain from c. 800 to the present day, a rich social history in today’s multicultural context. Pupils then examine Weimar and Nazi Germany, c. 1918-39, a poignant case study in how a nation can turn from a democracy to a dictatorship in a short space of time. This is followed by Superpower relations and the Cold War, c. 1941-91, and a British depth study on Early Elizabethan England, c. 1558-88. Pupils build skills as they work on the explanation of concepts and analysis and evaluation of sources and interpretations.
Geography stimulates an interest in and a sense of wonder about places, helping young people make sense of a complex and dynamically changing world. It explains how places and landscapes are formed, how people and their environment interact, and how a diverse range of economies, societies and environments are interconnected. Pupils develop a broad range of skills and we aim to ensure they complete at least one fieldwork investigation in each school year.
The Cambridge IGCSE Geography course gives pupils a solid grounding in all traditional topics in Geography, as well as the chance to demonstrate their understanding of map reading and completing a geographical investigation.
At Thames pupils are taught to engage positively with other people. Learning to listen, seeking to understand, and respecting others’ faiths and worldviews is essential. The Key Stage 3 curriculum prepares pupils for adult life by teaching them about the major world religions.
Religious Studies GCSE is taken in Year 10 and focuses on Christianity, Judaism and Christian ethics.
Business Studies introduces the dynamic, fast-paced world of commerce, developing the practical skills and theoretical knowledge to understand how organizations operate, adapt, and succeed in a global economy. Following the Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies syllabus, this two-year course from Year 10 provides a hands-on exploration of the real decisions facing modern entrepreneurs and global corporations alike. Topics include Business Activity & Ownership, People in Business, Marketing, Operations Management, Financial Information & Decisions.
Business Studies is far more than just theory; it is a springboard for real-world application. It develops vital analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills as pupils learn to evaluate actual business case studies and tackle contemporary economic challenges. Whether pupils dream of launching their own startup, pursuing a career in finance, marketing, management, or law, or simply want to understand the economic forces shaping daily life, Business Studies builds an solid foundation for higher education and future professional success.
It provides a base from which pupils can pursue Business Studies or Economics at A level as well as applying their knowledge to self-employment and business leadership in the future.
In Year 7 pupils study either Spanish or French. As they move through Years 8 and 9 gifted linguists have the opportunity to add the second language both of which can be studied at GCSE and onto A Level. An introduction to Mandarin and Chinese culture is taught as part of life skills in Year 9.
From Key Stage 3 through to GCSE, lessons are fast-paced, immersive and fun – blending games, music, authentic video, role-play and real cultural content with rigorous grammar teaching. Beyond the classroom, students get hands-on with culture through cooking workshops, making everything from Spanish tortilla to French crêpes and Chinese dumplings, and our Mandarin students head out on a trip to Chinatown to see the language and culture come alive on the streets.
Pupils don’t just memorise vocabulary; they learn to think in another language, building the confidence to hold conversations, understand native speakers and express themselves with growing accuracy across speaking, listening, reading and writing. Learning a language rewires how they see the world – sharpening memory, boosting problem-solving, and opening their eyes to cultures beyond their own.
Bilingual pupils may take GCSEs in their second language in Year 8, 9 or 10. These have recently included Russian, Modern Greek, Mandarin and Japanese.
Overseas trips give pupils the opportunity to practise using their language skills and broaden their cultural understanding. Past language trips include Iceland, Madrid, Barcelona, Malaga, Naples and Paris.
The Year 7 and 8 curriculum focuses on hardware, software, the Internet, AI, e-safety, digital art, and coding in Scratch and Python. Pupils who choose the subject in Year 9 dig deeper into Python programming and begin to learn the fundamentals of Boolean logic, data representation, computer architecture and cyber security. This serves as a foundation to the IGCSE in Computer Science, which is offered in Years 10 and 11. In 2026 a pupil was awarded first place in the ISA KS4 coding competition. Students are encouraged to think deeply about ethical issues and to develop career-ready skills through projects such as up-cycling used chromebooks, exploring the limits of AI, or developing advanced programming projects for entry into coding competitions.
Every pupil is gifted and at Thames we work hard to identify and stretch the gifting of each and every one whether it be in academics, visual and performing arts or on the sports field or several of those areas.

“As far as possible, leaders design personalised pathways for pupils, especially at A level, through subject choices which match pupils’ aptitudes and interests.”
Sixth Form Academic
At Thames there is a strategic focus on subjects that open doors to a range of degree choices and other options.
We recognise that students will take different pathways post-18 and we help and prepare them accordingly. Some students will choose the more traditional university route while others will apply to foundation courses or degree apprenticeships, and some may go straight into the workplace. Subject combinations are highly flexible and, as far as possible, these are tailored to the aspirations of each individual student. Tutorial sized classes are taught by highly skilled subject specialists with extensive experience of teaching A level. Many bring industry experience and expertise into the classroom.
Our 2026 leavers achieved 52% of A level grades at A*-A and 83% at A*-B.
Almost all subjects that ran for this cohort saw top A*/A grades including Mathematics, Further Mathematics, Physics, English Literature, History, Economics, Spanish, Art and 3D Design.
Recent destinations have included Exeter, Bath, Cardiff, Swansea, Manchester, Sheffield, Queen Mary University of London, Surrey, Essex, Kingston, Nottingham Trent, Goldsmiths and Oxford Brookes along with City & Guilds Art School. Some students move onto sought after degree apprenticeships whilst others find work placements related to their chosen careers.
Recent courses have included Architecture, Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science, Product Design, Biomedical Sciences, Accounting, Economics & Financial Mathematics, Psychology, Public Health and International Politics & Spanish.
Art and 3D Design are particularly strong with 75% of grades at A*/A and a number of students receiving unconditional university offers. The crossover between Maths, Physics and 3D Design has been a highly successful combination.
Students benefit from a brand new state of the art learning environment which includes: science laboratories designed for A Levels, a theatre with top of the range sound and lighting, design and STEAM workshops equipped with laser cutter, 3D printing, pressure former and mechanical and hand tools and art studios with a kiln. Students have exclusive use of a sixth form common room, independent study centre and seminar rooms.
Sixth form students at Thames sit three or four A Levels alongside full involvement in the wider activities offered. Subject specific trips enrich the A Level programme, making the most of the resources that London has to offer.
To study A Level subjects, students should have at least grade 7s at GCSE in those subjects as well as good passes in at least six other subjects including English and Maths.
Subjects are subject to minimum numbers and will reflect the range of interests of each cohort of students. This means that not all subjects will run in a given year.
Three-Dimensional Design A level is an exciting and creative course that helps facilitate varied careers in design and the wider visual arts. 80% of pupils completing the course have been offered places on related degree courses, including furniture and product design as well as several who have gone on to study architecture degrees, engineering courses and a related degree apprenticeship. During the course, students hear from a wide range of visiting designers who help them understand these varied career pathways. We also undertake relevant trips and practical workshops from visiting the London Design Festival to popular jewellery making workshops.
A series of varied briefs help students develop a broad skill base that includes traditional processes such as steam bending wood and joint making in the Arts and Crafts Chair project, to use of cutting edge computer aided design and manufacturing processes in making Bluetooth Speakers. Other Year 12 projects include an architectural “Modernist Escape” project, consideration of sustainable design in the Mycelium Design project and exploration of structural engineering principles through the Tensegrity project. Throughout these projects, students learn about key designers and ideas that have shaped the evolution of design over the past 150 years.
Year 13 builds on this foundation as students develop increasingly refined and ambitious work. In doing so, we are proud to say that 80% of students who have completed the Three Dimensional Design A Level at Thames achieved A*-A, and 100% were awarded A*-B.
A level Art is largely studio based and each student has their own personal space in which to work in a dedicated 6th form studio. Students are encouraged to study a wide variety of artists’ work and to develop their work according to their own ideas. They learn how to use a variety of media to a very high level. Students visit galleries in London and respond to the work of established artists with sophistication.
In the last two years 50% of grades have been at A* and 100% A*-B. Students have gained places at Kingston University, Nottingham Trent University and Loughborough University to study Architecture, Kingston University to study Product and Furniture Design and City and Guilds Foundation Course. The student who completed her Foundation Course at City and Guilds has taken up a place at Goldsmiths College, University of London
Biology A Level increases students’ knowledge and understanding of the study of living organisms and factors that may affect them. While developing their technical and practical skills, the course is designed to help students understand how decisions are made regarding scientific issues, and how the sciences contribute to the success of society as a whole. The Biology laboratory has been designed with A Levels in mind.
Biology A Level gives students career options including medicine, psychology, marine biology, biomedical science, sports science, nature conservation, pharmacology, environmental science and soil science.
Chemistry A Level enhances students’ knowledge and understanding of the properties of matter and how atoms, molecules and compounds interact to form the endless diversity of substances that make up our world. While developing their technical and practical skills, the course is designed to help students understand how decisions are made regarding scientific issues, and how the sciences contribute to the success of society as a whole. The Chemistry laboratory has been designed with A Levels in mind.
A Level Chemistry is a requirement for almost all university courses in medicine and veterinary science and many other science-related and STEM subjects.
Facilitated by highly knowledgeable teachers, students explore the three A Level components in an exciting and innovative way. Practical workshops include Theatre Practitioners such as Meisner, Utta Hagan, Berkoff, Artaud, Stanislavski, Brecht and more. (With Uta Hagen included on the approved practitioner list in 2025 due to exploration completed at Thames for our first A-Level cohort). We explore the set texts of Colder Than Here and Hedda Gabler for the written exam in year 13. An in-depth practical exploration of these texts enables deep understanding of the concepts and interpretations.
Students are encouraged to visit the theatre often to develop their love of the theatre and critical / analytical skills, and personalised, challenging lessons equip pupils with the skills necessary to succeed not only in their exams, but if they want to pursue a career in the industry.
Economics A Level gives a strong grounding in both micro- and macro-economics, and applies both to the modern world, making it topical and engaging. It helps students develop the skills, knowledge and understanding that will enable them to think and reason as economists. No prior learning or knowledge of economics is required for taking A Level Economics. Economics combines the benefits of both science and arts courses, with students having to write extensively as well as utilising their numeracy skills. Economics provides a good grounding for later life and can lead to careers in finance, banking, stock broking, law, politics and journalism.
The English Literature A Level at Thames follows the OCR syllabus, which rigorously challenges our students to think critically, and to develop an assertive literary angle. We tackle a range of texts which explore some of the deepest aspects of the human heart and society: Hamlet’s existential questioning; George Orwell’s scathing political satire, Nineteen Eighty Four; Rossetti’s Christian faith expressed in her poetry, for example. Through the study of other texts by authors from diverse backgrounds they develop the highly transferable skills of sustained research and critical evaluation through different literary lenses, while strengthening their own position and critique.
Contextual influences past and present are examined and woven into arguments, ensuring broad understanding and well positioned literary discussion. Thames English Literature pupils end year 13 confidently capable beyond literary debate: they leave with a firm emergent voice and a deep understanding of how to ‘read’ literature.
The Extended Project Qualification is worth 50% of an A Level but goes beyond A Level in terms of the research and skills involved and is a good preparation for university. It is recommended for students who are thriving in their three A Levels as it is a challenging step up.
The Extended Project will develop and extend from one or more of the student’s study areas and/or from an area of personal interest or activity outside their main programme of study. To complete the EPQ requires in total 120 hours project work in which a student can pursue their own line of enquiry and interest, having agreed their project with their supervisor.
A Level French takes students from confident communicators to true linguists—reading literature, debating ideas, and engaging with the culture and politics of the Francophone world with real sophistication.
Following the AQA specification, our students explore themes from France’s political landscape—including Maréchal Pétain’s Vichy regime, the Resistance movement, and modern political tensions around union power and immigration—to social issues such as life for the marginalised, evolving family structures, and the impact of the cyber-society. Students study books such as Mathieu Kassovitz’s La Haine in depth, developing the analytical precision to write and speak about complex ideas with real nuance.
Speaking is at the heart of the course. Students build towards the AQA oral exam through regular debate and a rich Independent Research Project discussion bank, while translation and essay writing sharpen accuracy in equal measure.
Beyond the exam, A Level French is a genuine passport—to study, work and travel across nearly 30 Francophone countries, and to a global language that opens doors in law, business, diplomacy, international relations, journalism and beyond.
Geography is a subject that links to many others such as economics, history and sociology, or biology, chemistry and maths. A student with a curiosity about the world around them – the patterns they see and the reasons for them, as well as the relationship between environment and society – is almost bound to do well. Geography students are in high demand in all areas of employment because of their training in data analysis and critical thinking. Geography provides an excellent skill basis for the majority of university degrees.
A Level History provides an ideal curriculum for students to ignite and engage their passions and interests. They will develop critical and reflective thinking, which they demonstrate in an essay exploring a topic of their own choosing, creating independent learners, critical thinkers and decision-makers. History is a highly respected academic subject and its strong emphasis on structured argument and source interrogation makes it an ideal preparation for university-level study in humanities, law, and social sciences.
The A Level course covers the periods of the French Revolution and Napoleon, Britain, 1930-1997 and Civil Rights in the USA along with an independent research essay where students select a historical debate of their choice, evaluating primary sources and conflicting secondary interpretations to construct a sustained argument.
A passion for mathematics lies at the heart of our teaching. Maths is viewed as a powerful language that unlocks the world around us. Our approach builds secure foundations, sharp problem-solving skills, and the confidence to tackle complex, unfamiliar challenges with independence. By bringing the subject to life in this way, we spark a deep curiosity that leads many of our students to choose Mathematics at A Level.
Throughout our A Level Mathematics course, students master structured logical reasoning, mathematical proof, and real-world problem solving. Alongside standard A Level scientific calculators, we provide guidance to help students explore graphing software and digital tools that deepen conceptual understanding. The curriculum covers Pure Mathematics—including calculus, trigonometry, vectors, sequences, and series—as well as Applied Mathematics, which encompasses Statistics (data analysis and probability) and Mechanics (forces, motion, and real-world modeling).
For ambitious students seeking an extra challenge, we also offer Further Mathematics at A Level. This course expands into fascinating advanced topics such as Complex Numbers, Matrices, Advanced Calculus, and Differential Equations. It serves as an essential prerequisite for degree-level Maths and significantly strengthens university applications for competitive fields like Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, and Economics.
